question.text: Which one of the following statements regarding Henry's law is not correct?

options.text: The value of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow></msub></math> changes with the nature of the gas.

Higher the value of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow></msub></math> at a given pressure, higher is the solubility of the gas in the liquids
The partial pressure of the gas in vapour phase is proportional to the mole fraction of the gas in the solution.

Different gases have different  <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow></msub></math>  (Henry's law constant) value at the same temperature.

solution.text:
Liquid solution Pgas=KH×Xgas as KH∝1Xgas
So, more is KH less is solubility. Solubility of gases is less at higher temperature. So more is the temperature more is the KH as KH∝1solubility∝ temperature
